text:
Tom (runtime): FYI hitting intermittent perf regressions on multi-GPU runs. Looks like comm/compute overlap disappears when KV cache hot path + cudaGraph capture are enabled. NVTX trace shows long idle gaps around all-reduce. Paging @Priya

Priya (perf): Can you paste the trace and a short repro? NVTX/CUPTI snapshots would help. Also what's NCCL/CUDA and whether this is Dedicated or local?

Tom (runtime): Repro on Dedicated (8xA100). CUDA 11.8, NCCL 2.15. Quick excerpt from trace: 
```
# nvtx timeline (simplified)
[0.0] stream0: matmul_fwd (compute)  -> 0.0-3.2ms
[3.2] stream0: cudaGraph capture begin
[3.2] stream1: kv_prefetch (async) -> 3.3-3.5ms
[3.5] stream0: allReduce (comm) blocked -> 3.5-7.8ms
[7.8] stream0: matmul_fwd (compute) resumes -> 7.8-10.1ms
# notice gap where compute waits on allReduce during capture region
```
link: https://internal.perf/reports/1945/trace-xyz

Dan (sre): Is UCX enabled? Also did this start after any infra change (driver, container base, nccl)?

Tom (runtime): UCX yes. No infra churn in last deploy window, but we did land a kernel-selection change two days ago that swaps to a smaller tiling kernel for certain sequence lengths.

Priya (perf): Hypothesis: cudaGraph capture is serializing stream semantics or pinning work to the capture stream so async comm can't overlap. Two quick experiments: 
1) disable cudaGraph for KV/attention paths 
2) force capture on a low-priority stream and set comm on high-priority stream (or vice versa)

Tom (runtime): Ran quick perf:
- capture on default stream: throughput 860 tok/s, p95 latency 210ms
- capture disabled for kv path: throughput 980 tok/s, p95 175ms
Surprising: capture hurts overlap here ~12% throughput drop.

Marta (ml): The kernel-selection change could make matmul longer, increasing compute window so all-reduce sits in the gap. Also some quantized kernels have different stream-sync behavior. Which kernel version are you landing?

Tom (runtime): It's the tiling fallback commit (hash: a1f3b2). Matmul runtime time increased ~8% on local microbench. Might be compounding with capture behavior.

Priya (perf): Can you run with NVTX around these hot ops and also capture cudaMemcpy/async timings? Also try toggling stream priorities:
```
# set NVTX markers and run
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0
# run with env to force capture on stream 2 (low priority)
REDWOOD_CUDA_GRAPH_STREAM=2 REDWOOD_STREAM_PRI_LOW=2 make run-repro
```

Tom (runtime): Will do. I also suspect NCCL schedule: if capture holds a stream that NCCL expects, allreduce is serialized. I'll try reproducing with a tiny micro-bench that does: matmul -> allreduce -> matmul under capture vs no-capture.

Dan (sre): Also check for cudaGraph fallback paths in mixed capture cases. There are known issues where captured graph replays on a single stream and kernels enqueued to other streams are synchronized.

Priya (perf): If you can push the micro-repro and perf trace to the perf bucket I can run cupy/nvprof and look for cross-stream syncs. If it's a regression from kernel-selection, we can revert the tiling change or add a guard when cudaGraph capture is enabled.

Tom (runtime): Pushed repro + trace to https://internal.perf/reports/1945/micro-repro.tar.gz. Next steps: run nvprof with `--print-gpu-trace --csv` and capture CUPTI timeline. I'll also try disabling cudaGraph for kv-prefetch by feature flag.

deploy-bot: build/8942 deployed to infra:dedicated-us-west-1 (no infra changes to driver or container) :rocket:

Marta (ml): Another angle: batching heuristics might increase sequence variance so more items hit the tiling edge case making compute longer. Check batching distribution in the repro too.

Tom (runtime): Good call. I'll include per-batch seq len histogram. Will report numbers by EOD.

Priya (perf): Great. If we confirm capture is the culprit, we should document a runtime guard: autodisable cudaGraph when KV prefetch + certain kernels are active, or capture on explicitly isolated streams. Thanks for flagging. :thumbsup:

Tom (runtime): Thanks — sending updates after the NVTX/CUPTI run.
